data.title: Business Tempo and Events Disclose Timing Opportunities
data.summary:
Published financial calendars, event attendance, supplier announcements and recruitment
activity disclose when the organisation is distracted, when staff are travelling and when
unusual requests are expected.
data.description:
Timing is what makes a pretext land. A payment request during a known acquisition, an
IT instruction during a published migration, or an urgent approval while the signatory is
at a conference all arrive when they are plausible and when the person who would normally
check is unavailable.

Most of this information is published deliberately and for good reasons — results dates,
conference attendance, supplier partnerships — so the exposure cannot be removed by
withholding it.

What can be changed is the organisation's assumption that unusual requests during unusual
periods are explained by the period. That assumption is precisely what is being exploited.
data.recommendation:
* Raise verification requirements during known high-exposure periods rather than relaxing
  them for convenience.
* Brief finance and executive support staff ahead of published events, with the specific
  pretexts that fit the period.
* Avoid publishing individual travel and attendance in advance where it is not necessary.
data.short_recommendation: Raise verification requirements during published high-exposure periods.
